From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial ask: RTO/RPO evidence for SOC2 + SIG intake

Alex / team — adding technical detail on RTO/RPO guarantees and what the evidence will show. Paste below is intended for your SIG/SOC reviewers.

1) What we guarantee (short):
- Persistent state (model binaries, metadata): replicated across AZs, persisted to object storage with cross-region replication options for Dedicated customers (configurable). RPO for persisted state: 0 (no loss) once snapshot completes; snapshot cadence documented.
- In-flight inference state (KV/cache, session context): we provide best-effort prefix/KV caching to accelerate latency. For Hosted API we maintain warm-prefix caches in our warm-standby in-region pool; following an AZ failover we rehydrate prefixes from persistent traces — RPO target for cache: <= 1 minute for most workloads but depends on session TTLs.

2) What the artifacts will include:
- rto_rpo_snapshot-20260801.pdf: annotated timeline of the 08/01 drill (step-by-step, timestamps).
- runbook-extracts-ops.txt: activation steps, runbook excerpts, escalation matrix.
- s3-retention-log-sample.csv: sanitized object-store logs showing last 30 days retention/restore samples.

3) Notes for reviewers:
- Our inference runtime uses continuous batching + KV checkpointing; the artifacts include the script we use to generate the checkpoint export used in restores. We'll redact any customer IDs.
- For Dedicated customers requiring stronger RPO we offer more frequent snapshotting and optional cross-region replication; we can provide a configuration snapshot for your account if needed (that will include your Dedicated pool name).

If you want deeper telemetry (traces of token-level replay during warm-start) we can include a short 5-minute clip of telemetry traces under NDA.

-Karthik
Principal Applied ML Eng — Redwood Inference

1) The RTO figures look good; can you confirm whether the Hosted API RTO measurement includes DNS propagation time for region failovers or if that's measured from our edge to your control-plane handoff? Our vendor reviewer asks for the exact start/stop criteria.

3) For Dedicated pools: can you share the shortest and longest observed re-assignment times from the last 6 months (even a small table is fine)? That helps our risk model.

If you can reply with short bullets by EOD tomorrow we'll close our review and proceed to the SIG questionnaire.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
